findings.title: Native-main callback into Go may block
findings.message: The native callback `vellumTitlebarAction` is invoked synchronously on the AppKit main thread and takes accessibilityRegistry lock and calls PostWindow. If PostWindow blocks (bounded queue), it could stall the main thread. Also vellumTitlebarAllowed uses dispatch_async while Go-side setAllowed flips state immediately, so permission in Go and native `allowed` can diverge transiently.
findings.suggestion: Confirm PostWindow is non-blocking; keep native `allowed` authoritative only as UI state and rely on Go permission for gating.

findings.title: Detach silently no-ops off main thread
findings.message: vellumTitlebarDetach returns early if not on the main thread, silently leaking the toolbar and registry entry. closeTitlebarToolbar in Go is called from accessibilityAttachment.Close and the attach-failure path; if those run off the main thread, detach never happens and the registry (limit 1) stays occupied.
findings.suggestion: Dispatch to the main queue when not on main thread (dispatch_sync/async) instead of returning.

findings.title: Owner window/token assignment unclear; detach may not remove toolbar
findings.message: On attach failure paths after the owner is registered in vellumTitlebars (e.g. the final `return window.contentView==view && window.toolbar==toolbar`), the Go side calls vellumTitlebarDetach. But the earlier early-returns before registration are fine; the problem is that Detach runs `owner.window` which is weak and `owner.window` is never assigned in the visible code (the line is redacted/truncated), so restoring window.toolbar may be skipped, leaving the toolbar attached to a window after detach.
findings.suggestion: Ensure owner.window=window and owner.token=token are set explicitly on separate statements before registering the owner.
